note: Every distinct capability in the fal non-generation catalogue, paired with a source chosen so the effect is actually visible. The trap this guards against: running a restoration tool on a clean image and calling the identical output a demonstration. Where an effect only reads at full magnification, `crop` says so.

sources.prompt: Full-length editorial photograph of a person standing in a bare plaster room, wearing loose oatmeal linen, arms relaxed and slightly away from the body, one knee bent, head turned three-quarters to camera, raking north light, warm neutral palette, matte, medium format

A genuine black-and-white silver gelatin photograph from the 1950s: a woman in a wool coat standing beside a parked car on a wet cobbled street, soft grey tonal range, visible film grain, absolutely no colour anywhere in the frame, documentary photography

A very high-ISO night photograph of a dimly lit bar interior, heavy luminance and chroma noise across the whole frame, grainy shadows, muddy dark tones, handheld, ISO 12800, visibly noisy digital photograph

A stoneware bottle on a white surface lit by a single hard undiffused flash from the upper right, producing a harsh black shadow with a razor edge, blown highlights on the shoulder of the bottle, unflattering direct light, product photograph badly lit

A simple flat vector wordmark on a plain bone-white ground: the word SALVAGE in a heavy geometric sans-serif, deep olive, beneath it a single horizontal rule and a small circular monogram, absolutely flat solid colour with no gradients, no texture, no photography, logo artwork

demos.why: A mask from a description, with no clicking and no hand-drawn box. It feeds straight into an edit call's mask parameter, which is what makes the rest of the catalogue composable.
demos.title: A mask from a phrase

demos.why: Every region at once rather than one you named. Use it to inventory an unfamiliar image before deciding what to act on.
demos.title: Every region at once

opts.prompt: How many bottles are there, and what is the vessel on the right made of?

demos.why: Reads an image into an answer. The cheapest way to branch a pipeline on what a picture actually contains.
demos.title: Ask a question about a picture

demos.why: Open-vocabulary detection: boxes for anything you can name, without training a detector for it.
demos.title: Find anything you can name

demos.why: Type out of a photograph as text. The step before you can search, index or re-set what a picture says.
demos.title: Read the type off a photograph

demos.why: Distance encoded as brightness. Feed it to a ControlNet-style model to regenerate a scene while keeping its geometry.
demos.title: Distance as brightness

demos.why: A body reduced to a skeleton. Hold a figure's stance steady while everything else about the image changes.
demos.title: A body as a skeleton

demos.why: Contour without tone or colour. Carries composition into a restyle that would otherwise drag the original palette with it.
demos.title: Contour without colour

demos.why: Surface direction per pixel. The input a renderer needs to light a flat photograph as though it had relief.
demos.title: Surface direction per pixel

demos.why: A cut-out on transparency. The first step of any composite, and the reason alpha matters more than resolution here.
demos.title: Cut out to transparency

demos.why: Take an object out and rebuild what was behind it. Cheap, and it leaves what the object did to the light.
demos.title: Remove an object for $0.024

demos.why: The same removal including the object's shadow and its caustic. Eleven times the price, and the only version that survives a second look.
demos.title: Remove its shadow too, for $0.27

demos.why: Strip the words and keep the surface. Useful when the artwork is right and the copy is not.
demos.title: Strip the words, keep the surface

demos.why: Invent canvas beyond the frame. For when a crop is tight and reframing would cut something you need.
demos.title: Invent canvas beyond the frame

demos.why: One image into another ratio without regenerating it. Regenerating gives you a different picture; this gives you the same one, differently shaped.
demos.title: A new ratio, the same picture

demos.why: Detail recovered rather than pixels stretched. Judge it at full magnification or you are judging the thumbnail.
demos.title: Detail recovered, not stretched

demos.why: Sensor noise removed without taking the texture with it. The failure mode of a bad denoiser is wax, so look at the grain, not the whole frame.
demos.title: Noise gone, texture kept

demos.why: Plausible colour for a monochrome original. It is an interpretation, not a recovery: nothing in the negative knows what colour the coat was.
demos.title: Colour for a monochrome original

demos.why: Harsh directional light flattened to an even base. What you want before compositing a product into a scene with different lighting.
demos.title: Take the light out

opts.prompt: soft diffused north window light from the left, gentle falloff, no hard shadow

demos.why: Light the shot again after it was taken. Cheaper than reshooting and the only option when the subject is gone.
demos.title: Put different light back

demos.why: A scene taken apart into named objects plus the emptied room behind them. Re-compose without regenerating anything.
demos.title: A scene as named objects

demos.why: The plate with the type lifted off, and the type returned as positions and fonts. For changing what a finished design says.
demos.title: Type lifted off a design

demos.why: Pixels to paths. Scales to any size, edits as shapes, and prints without a resolution argument.
demos.title: Pixels to paths

demos.why: A photograph of a surface becomes the five maps a renderer needs to light it. Photograph a material once, use it in 3D forever.
demos.title: Five maps from one photograph

opts.prompt: seamless undyed linen weave, natural oat, flat even light

demos.why: A texture that repeats without a visible seam. The difference between a photograph of fabric and a material you can apply.
demos.title: A texture that repeats

demos.why: A mesh from a single photograph. Not a scan, but enough geometry to place a real object into a rendered scene. The mesh itself is not kept in the repository - it is 15MB of geometry that nothing on a page can render. Regenerate it with scripts/run-demos.mjs.
demos.title: A mesh from a single photograph

demos.why: A sub-cent gate for a pipeline that publishes what it generates. Returns a probability, not a decision.
demos.title: Gate a pipeline for a fraction of a penny
